program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or standard; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: MD4 of the 7 strings in the RFC 1320 test suite ("", "a", "abc", "message digest", the lowercase alphabet, upper+lower+digits, and 80 digits) gives the 7 published 128-bit digests

expected_values_source.what: the 7 digests of the test suite in RFC 1320 section A.5
expected_values_source.note: the digests are data, copied as numbers; the RFC's reference code was not copied

negative_control: built with -DMD4_K3=0x6ed9eba2u (one bit of the round-3 constant changed), 0 of 7 digests match and the program exits 1
not_checked: security claims: MD4 is broken (collisions are easy); this only shows the algorithm as published gives the published digests
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
inputs other than those listed in the RFC test suite (no multi-block streaming or long-message tests)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 7 MD4 digests published in RFC 1320. It does not show MD4 is secure (it is not).
